payload.answer: Pass timeout=(connect, read) to requests, e.g. requests.get(url, timeout=(3.05, 27)). The connect timeout limits how long to wait to establish the TCP connection; the read timeout limits how long to wait between bytes from the server. A single number applies to both. By default requests has no timeout and can hang indefinitely.

results.title: Advanced Usage — Requests 2.32.3 documentation
results.snippet: The connect timeout is the number of seconds Requests will wait for your client to establish a connection to a remote machine (corresponding to the connect()) call on the socket. It's a good practice to set connect timeouts to slightly larger than a multiple of 3, which is the default TCP packet retransmission window. Once your client has connected to the server and sent the HTTP request, the read timeout is the number of seconds the client will wait for the server to send a response.

payload.content: In the Python requests library, the `timeout` argument accepts either a single number or a `(connect, read)` tuple. The connect timeout is how long to wait while establishing the connection; the read timeout is how long to wait for the server to send data once connected, measured between bytes rather than for the whole download. For example `requests.get(url, timeout=(3.05, 27))`. If you omit it, requests does not time out at all.
